facts.text: Fall Creek takes its name from a nearby creek of the same name, which was named for a waterfall along its course.
By 1831, the creek’s waters powered grist mills, and by the 19th century it remained a vital element for milling and agriculture.
The first sawmill appeared in 1824, powered by Fall Creek, and early settlers built schools, churches, and organized marriages along its banks.
Fall Creek sits in Adams County, northwestern Illinois, about three miles southwest of Payson and 12 miles south of Quincy, near the Mississippi River Valley.
The creek’s cascading waterfalls now form the Fall Creek Scenic Overlook, drawing visitors to bluffs overlooking the Mississippi River.
